html:
The Quechan, long called the Yuma, are a Native American people of the lower Colorado River, where the Gila River joins it, on today's border of Arizona and California. They speak a Yuman language.

They farmed the floodplain, planting maize, beans and melons in the mud left by the yearly floods, and they were known as warriors. Their land held the main river crossing on the land route between Sonora and California, the Yuma Crossing.

Juan Bautista de Anza crossed with their help in 1774 and 1775, and Spain built two missions among them in 1780. In 1781 the Quechan rose, destroyed both missions and killed the soldiers and priests there. The revolt closed the overland road to Spanish California for the rest of colonial rule. Americans built Fort Yuma at the crossing in 1850. See also Quechan on the modern map.
